description: A build without the TCF decoder (--no-tcf, for deployments that never need TCF). A TC string isn't decoded, so it denies storage exactly as an unreadable one does, whatever gdpr says, with its own reason, and deletes existing ID cookies: a TC string that would allow storage in the default build never does here. Where GDPR applies from the location (Germany here) without a TC string, storage is denied as in every build; elsewhere without a TC string the ID is set. TC string: CAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA.eAAAAAAAAA has publisher consent for purposes 1-2 (the default build sets the ID with it; see consent.json). Requests describe the location with Cloudflare's visitor location headers, as in consent-eu-location.json.

cases.name: GDPR applies (gdpr=1): a TC string with publisher consent sets nothing

headers.x-sharedid-status: denied: tcf: TC string not decoded (build without TCF)

cases.name: GDPR applies from the location: the CMP's euconsent-v2 cookie sets nothing and existing ID cookies are deleted

headers.x-sharedid-status: denied: tcf: TC string not decoded (build without TCF)

cases.name: a TC string denies even with gdpr=0, as an unreadable one does

headers.x-sharedid-status: denied: tcf: TC string not decoded (build without TCF)

cases.name: GDPR applies from the location without a TC string: nothing is set, as in every build

headers.x-sharedid-status: denied: tcf: GDPR applies and there is no TC string

cases.name: outside the GDPR countries without a TC string, the ID is set
